title: Platform Modernisation at Northwind Logistics
subtitle: A fictional sample case study used to test Boku's report layout, charts, diagrams and citations
executive_summary: Northwind Logistics, a fictional carrier used here as test data, completed most of a migration of its dispatch platform to Kubernetes by the end of 2025, with 85% of dispatch services running on the new platform [F001]. The programme is best read as a cost and delivery-speed initiative rather than a technology refresh.

Unit infrastructure cost fell from $0.42 to $0.31 per shipment over two years [F002], and deployment frequency rose roughly fourfold [F004]. The deployment figure is derived from company-reported counts and rests on a single source, so it should be treated as indicative.
Management's savings target of about $18 million by 2027 is an estimate made in 2024 [F005]; no later confirmation was found.

key_findings.headline: The migration is largely complete
key_findings.detail: 85% of dispatch services ran on Kubernetes by December 2025 [F001].

key_findings.headline: Unit costs fell by about a quarter
key_findings.detail: Infrastructure cost per shipment declined from $0.42 in 2023 to $0.31 in 2025 [F002].

key_findings.headline: The industry is moving the same way
key_findings.detail: 61% of surveyed platform teams run production AI inference on Kubernetes [F003].

blocks.text: Northwind's dispatch system coordinated routing, carrier assignment and customer notifications. The company chose an incremental, service-by-service migration rather than a single cut-over [F001].
Incremental migration let the team keep the legacy system as a fallback throughout, which **reduced cut-over risk** at the cost of running two platforms for most of 2025 [F001].
Reported cost per shipment declined each year of the programme [F002].
The $18 million savings figure is management guidance from 2024, not a reported result [F005].
Northwind's direction matches the wider market: a 2026 survey found that most platform teams now run AI inference on Kubernetes [F003].

conclusion: The evidence supports a clear story: the migration is largely complete and unit costs have fallen [F001, F002]. What remains unproven is whether the 2027 savings estimate will be met [F005].
